answer.rationale: Prioritize referral incentives among established customers: they added qualified revenue without measurable retention harm. Do not broadly counter the competitor with promotional pricing; the recovered discount result showed a 12% 30-day retention decline despite acquisition and qualified-revenue gains, conflicting with the long-term revenue objective. Referral incentives are not proven to directly reduce current price-driven churn, so maintain that uncertainty and target the proven established-customer segment.
